cycles.name: Bedrock
focuses: Learn the big lifts properly: squat, hinge and split squat, light and filmed.
Quiet landings, pull-up and dip baselines, and a daily protein habit.

paragraphs: Welcome in, Behnam. This first block is called Bedrock. You've trained for years with your bodyweight, but the bar is new, so these 5 weeks are about learning the big lifts properly. Light on purpose, filmed, done right.

Your padel is already your speed and endurance training. Nobody can out-train 5 or 6 days on court. What the court can't give you is muscle and real strength in your legs, and that is exactly the gym's job. We start with 3 gym days on purpose, so your legs can meet loading without stealing anything from your court play. Day 4 arrives next block.
By the end of Bedrock you'll move weight with confidence, your legs will already feel different, and we'll have real numbers to build everything else on.
outcomes: Squat, hinge and split squat learned and filmed clean
First loaded numbers on the board
Pull-up and dip baselines set in week 1

cycles.name: First Iron
focuses: The bar starts moving on both leg patterns: small steady load jumps, week after week.
Weighted pull-ups begin, and the low positions and jumping you asked for start here.

paragraphs: Five weeks ago you had never put a weight on your back. Your goblet squat went from 8 kg to 14 kg and every video you sent me was clean. So the bar is yours now. Your dumbbells got easy on the hinge too, and they're gone.

You told me you want to sit lower at the back of the court and stay down there. That's not a fitness thing. It's strength in a position you've never trained. So now we stop at the bottom of everything. The squat, the split squat, the wall sit. That low position is the whole point of this block.
The jumping starts too. Not a lot of it, but real ones every session, and medicine ball throws for your swing.
outcomes: Barbell squat and hinge loaded, filmed and clean
First weighted pull-ups on the board
Sitting deeper, and holding it longer
Your dip max finally on paper
Landings quiet and stuck on one leg
Food and body weight logged every day

cycles.name: Structural Build
focuses: Lower-body muscle building: the volume block your legs asked for.
Fueled by the eating habit built in blocks 1 and 2.

paragraphs: Next block is Structural Build. It's the one you asked me for on day one, when you told me your legs were weak and you wanted them bigger.
That's the volume block. More work, more food, more size.
But it only pays you back if your eating is steady by the time it starts. That part is on you, and it starts now.
Feed the legs and they'll grow.

cycles.name: Strength Engine
focuses: Heavy lower-body strength: less volume, more weight moving.
Upper strength peaks with weighted pull-up and dip bests.

cycles.name: Power Transfer
focuses: Explosive power at low volume and maximal intent: strength turned into court speed.
Back to three gym days; the extra day goes to your padel.

days.completionMessage: First barbell squats done, and every pause at the bottom is you buying a lower defensive position. Eat something proper and let the court have you tomorrow.

good: Find an easy steady rhythm
Stay tall and springy on the balls of your feet
bad: Don't hunch over the rope

good: Reach for the ceiling on the twist
Feel the front hip open up
bad: Don't let the back knee drop inward

good: Drive the knee out over the little toe
Feel the stretch low in the calf
bad: Don't let the heel lift off the floor

good: Push the floor away with your heels
Squeeze the glutes at the top
bad: Don't arch the low back to go higher

good: Pull yourself down between your knees
Feel the hips and ankles loosen
bad: Don't round the back when you fold down

good: Push the floor away at the top
Feel the shoulder blades spread apart
bad: Don't bend the elbows, this is blades only

good: Sink to a low quarter and drive straight up off the floor
Feel the legs load like a spring before you go
bad: Don't land stiff-legged or let the knees fall inward

good: Bounce off the floor like it's hot, barely bend the knees
Feel it in the ankles and calves, not the thighs
bad: Don't sink into a squat between bounces

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.note: The bar is on your back now, and I know you already know this lift. Week 1 keep it at RPE 6 and just find your weight with the pause held still. The 1 second stop at the bottom is the whole exercise, that's your defending position. Any back complaint at all, go to the goblet squat and message me.

good: Push the floor apart and stand up tall
Feel the weight through the middle of your foot in the pause
bad: Don't round the low back at the bottom to get deeper

exercises.name: Strict Pull-Up
exercises.note: You did 13 clean ones at bodyweight, so around 10 kg on a belt should make a set of 6 genuinely hard. This is the only lift where you're adding weight upstairs this block.

good: Pull your chest to the bar
Feel the lats do the work, not the arms
bad: Don't kick or swing to finish a rep

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
exercises.note: New one, and it pulls hard on your groin at the bottom. Start with no weight and only go half way down. Get the depth first, then the weight. If your heel lifts, put a small plate under it or bring your feet closer.

good: Sit down into one hip and keep the other leg long on the floor
Feel the working hip and thigh take the weight
bad: Don't let the low back round to get lower

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.note: This is you defending at the back of the court, just standing still. Slide down until your thighs are flat and don't creep up when it burns.

good: Slide down until your thighs are flat and hold still
Feel the burn build in the front of the thighs
bad: Don't creep up higher when the burn builds, but if it turns into sharp pain at the front of the knee, stop the set

days.completionMessage: The bar moved on your hinge and you threw hard from the ground up. That's your swing getting a bigger engine behind it.

good: Find an easy steady rhythm
Stay tall and springy on the balls of your feet
bad: Don't hunch over the rope

good: Push the floor away as you round
Feel the spine move one bone at a time
bad: Don't force the end of the range

good: Turn both knees down to the floor together
Feel it deep in the hip
bad: Don't lean back to get there

good: Reach long, hand forward and heel back
Feel the trunk stay square
bad: Don't let the hips tip

good: Push your hips back and keep the dowel touching your head, back and hips
Feel the hamstrings take the stretch
bad: Don't let the dowel come off your low back

good: Pull the band apart to your chest
Feel the shoulder blades pull together
bad: Don't shrug the shoulders up

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
exercises.note: Your first real rotation work, so this block is about doing it right and doing it fast, not doing lots of it. Start the throw from the ground and your hip. If your low back says anything, throw easier and tell me.

good: Turn the back hip through and throw the ball at the wall
Feel it start from the ground and the hip, not the arm
bad: Don't arch your low back to get more turn

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.note: You smash enough overhead on court already, so we keep the throwing in front of you. Push it at the wall as hard as you can.

good: Push the ball at the wall as hard and as fast as you can
Feel the chest and triceps fire together
bad: Don't let the low back arch as you push

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: Your dumbbells got easy at 7.5 kg a hand, so the bar takes over. Brace before every rep like someone's about to poke your stomach. Week 1 stays at RPE 6. If your back complains, switch to the cable pull through and message me.

good: Push your hips back toward the wall behind you and keep the bar on your legs
Feel the hamstrings stretch just above the knee
bad: Don't round the back to go lower

exercises.name: Dip
exercises.note: We still don't have your dip number from last block. Week 1 do one honest max set at bodyweight and send me the number, then we add weight from week 2. Stop when your upper arms are level with the floor, never lower than that.

good: Push the bars down until the elbows lock
Feel the chest and triceps take it
bad: Don't drop your upper arms below parallel with the floor

exercises.name: Stability Ball Leg Curl
exercises.note: New, and it's here because your hamstrings need work that bends the knee, not just the hinge. Keep your hips up the whole time.

good: Pull your heels in toward your backside and keep the hips up
Feel the back of the thighs doing the pulling
bad: Don't let the hips drop as the ball comes in

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.note: Knee stays on the bench, not the foot. Only going from 15 to 18 seconds because your groin has a lot on this block already.

good: Drive the top knee down into the bench and lift the hips
Feel the inside of the top thigh working
bad: Don't let the hips drop toward the floor

days.completionMessage: Every quiet landing today is an ankle and a knee that won't fold on you when you're stretched wide at the back. Good session.

good: Keep an easy steady pace
Feel the legs warm up and the breathing pick up
bad: Don't turn this into a sprint

good: Swing the leg loose front to back
Feel the hip free up
bad: Don't arch the back to swing higher

good: Draw a big circle with the knee
Feel the hip move through its whole range
bad: Don't lean away to get round

good: Drive the knee out over the little toe
Feel the stretch low in the calf
bad: Don't let the heel lift off the floor

good: Step wide and keep the band tight
Feel the side of the hip
bad: Don't let the knees fall in

good: Push the hips back and sit into the stepping leg
Feel the inside of the straight leg stretch
bad: Don't let the knee cave inward

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.note: This is your first jump landing on one leg, so the landing is the exercise. Land quiet and freeze for 2 seconds before you go back. Do 15 or 20 easy bounces first to wake the legs up. Don't chase distance.

good: Push sideways off one leg, land quiet on the other and freeze for 2 seconds
Feel the outside of the landing leg catch you and hold
bad: Don't let the landing knee fall inward

exercises.name: Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.note: Front foot goes on a low step so you get deeper than last block. You sat at 10 kg all of Bedrock, so this time depth goes up before weight does.

good: Drop the back knee straight down toward the floor
Feel the front thigh and glute take the weight at the bottom
bad: Don't let the front knee drift inward

good: Row the dumbbell to your hip
Feel the shoulder blade pull down and back
bad: Don't twist your shoulders to lift it

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Single Leg Calf Raise
exercises.note: Loaded now, where last block was bodyweight. Your calves are carrying more jumping this time and they need to be ready for it.

good: Push the floor away through the big toe
Feel the stretch at the bottom before you drive up
bad: Don't bounce out of the bottom

good: Walk a straight line with your shoulders level
Feel the opposite side of your trunk fighting to stay upright
bad: Don't let your body tip toward the weight

cards.title: Week 1 is for finding your weights
cards.body:
The cards say RPE 7 on the squat and the RDL. Not in week 1. Week 1 you keep both at RPE 6 and just find the weight that lets you hold the pause still. From week 2 you go to the number on the card.

How you move it after that:

  • Hit all the reps at or under the target RPE, go up a small step next week.
  • Missed reps, or it felt harder than the target, stay on the same weight and do it again.
  • Bad day and you drop the weight? That's the system working, not you failing.

Last block you logged a few sessions as RPE 10 by mistake. The RPE is the target, not a score. 7 means you had 3 more reps in you.

cards.title: Film your top sets
cards.body:
Same deal as last block, and it worked. Film the last set of your squat and your RDL in weeks 1 and 2 and send them to me. The bar is new on both, so I want to see them before the weight climbs.

Also film one set of the Cossack squat before you ever hold a weight on it. That one is new and it stretches your groin at the bottom, so I want eyes on it first.

No film, no weight increase. Simple.

cards.title: Your back, your shoulder, and pain
cards.body:
Your back and shoulder are old news and this program keeps them that way. But the bar sits on your back now, so read this once properly.

Normal: muscle burn, feeling worked, stiff the next day. Train through it.

Not normal: sharp pain, pain shooting down a leg or arm, numbness or tingling, or pain that grows set by set.

  • Mild and fading? Finish the set and write it in your log.
  • Building, or changing how you move? Stop that exercise, do its backup, message me.
  • Sharp, shooting or numb? Stop the session and message me before the next one.

One more, because you're 16 and still growing and the jumping doubles this block. Pain at the front of your knee, in your heel, or along your shin bone that's there when you wake up or gets worse through a session means no jumping that day. Do the strength work only and tell me.

cards.title: Look after your groin
cards.body:
Three things this block pull on your groin. The Cossack squat, the Copenhagen plank, and the side jumps. Your padel does plenty too.

That's why the Copenhagen only goes from 15 seconds to 18, and why the Cossack starts with no weight and only half depth. One thing at a time. I'm not stacking them all at once.

Any tightness or a pull in there and both of them drop to their backup, and you message me. Don't push through a groin.

cards.title: When the week goes wrong
cards.body:
Your week won't be clean every time. Here's how to bend the plan instead of skipping it.

  • Low energy day: take 1 off every RPE, but never below 6. Anything already at 6 stays at 6.
  • No time: do the first big lift at RPE 6 plus one other exercise. That counts. Cut the jumps and throws first, never last. Tired jumping is how people get hurt.
  • Gym on a padel day: gym after padel, or leave 4 to 6 hours. If you can't, skip the jumps and throws completely and keep the lifting, primary at RPE 6.
  • Camp week: lifting only at RPE 6, no jumps and no throws. The camp already gives your legs more than the gym ever will.

Order is yours around your padel. Two rules only. Leave a day between Day 2 and Day 3, and don't put Day 1 and Day 3 back to back.

cards.title: Eat, and weigh yourself
cards.body:
You're 70 kg, you're 16, you're still growing, and you're doing 8 or 9 sessions a week between court and gym. Your food is the one thing you've never made consistent, and it's now the thing holding your legs back.

  • Eat before the gym session and again within an hour after.
  • Never do the gym day empty after padel.
  • Protein at every meal. Eggs, chicken, meat, yogurt, whatever is at home.

And turn on the weight tracker in the habit app and log your weight a few times a week. If you start dropping weight without meaning to, I need to see it early, especially with the jumping going up.

cards.title: What you already did
cards.body:
Two things from last block that are worth saying out loud.

Your goblet squat went 8 kg to 14 kg in five weeks and every video was clean. That's a proper first month with a weight in your hands.

And you did 13 strict pull-ups at 70 kg. That's a real number. Most people who lift for years don't have it. Your upper body isn't the problem, it never was, and this block finally starts loading it.

cards.title: Why there's jumping now
cards.body:
Last block I told you there were no jumps in your plan and that the court was your speed coach. That was true then. You had no strength to turn into speed yet.

It's different now. You've got a base, and you asked me for something specific, which is staying low at the back of the court for longer. So the jumps here are not extra running. They're about landing quietly, holding a low position, and pushing back out of it.

Still don't add your own jump or sprint sessions on top. What's in the plan is the right amount.

cards.title: Log it properly
cards.body:
You're the only one in the gym. Your log is the only way I see what happened, so it has to be honest.

Write the weight for every set. Pick the RPE that's true, not the highest one. And the readiness questions at the start actually matter, so answer them how you really feel, not all 5s.

Last block half the sessions went in as perfect and RPE 10 at the same time. I couldn't read anything from that.
